summary: A passing frontal boundary across coastal Miami-Dade County is generating scattered showers and thunderstorms near Turkey Point. The National Weather Service in Miami reported potential for heavy downpours and breezy conditions with northeasterly gusts reaching up to 32 mph. These conditions pose a minor storm hazard characterized by isolated convective gusts and localized runoff.

articles.title: NWS Forecast Office Miami - South Florida Weather Briefing
articles.snippet: Showers and thunderstorms are expected across Coastal Miami-Dade County, producing localized heavy rainfall and wind gusts reaching 30 to 32 mph.

articles.title: Oct. 17: Storms, strong winds & dangerous rip current ahead
articles.snippet: A cold front is moving through South Florida to trigger widespread showers and storms, accompanied by wind gusts exceeding 30 mph.

summary: A frontal boundary traversing South Florida is bringing elevated northeasterly winds and lingering isolated showers across coastal Miami-Dade County, producing peak gusts near 30 mph. Severe storm activity has subsided following the main weekend frontal passage, leaving limited convective thunderstorm risks and minor rainfall for the area. As a result, storm hazards at Turkey Point remain low to minor heading into Monday.
